name: health-export-ai
description: Query your Apple Health data, exported by the MetricBridge iOS app to iCloud Drive, from any MCP agent. Local-first, read-only, zero dependencies.
long_description: A zero-dependency MCP server that exposes 194 Apple Health metrics (exported by the MetricBridge iOS app into an iCloud Drive folder) to any MCP-compatible agent: Claude Desktop, opencode, Cursor, OpenClaw, Hermes. No bridge, no Docker, no HTTP receiver: the server reads the synced cache file directly over stdio. 18 tools: get_mcp_status, get_freshness, list_metrics, get_health_metrics, get_trends, compare_periods, get_structured_export, get_intraday, query_health_data, list_events, add_event, remove_event, get_profile, get_workouts, get_sleep_sessions, get_cycle_context, correlate_metrics, resolve_metric. Every tool is read-only except add_event and remove_event, which write only health-events-agent.json in the export folder (never Apple Health, never a file the app writes). Plus 22 MCP prompts and a --demo mode with a synthetic dataset. Get the companion iOS app on the App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/apple-store/id6784185201?pt=129083290&ct=githubreadme&mt=8&ppid=2c28f88a-d94f-48f9-8e6a-74a8d89ce66e

tools.name: get_mcp_status
tools.description: Health check: source, metric/workout counts, latest data date, freshness. Call first.

tools.name: get_freshness
tools.description: How current the export is: stale flag judged on the core files (daily cache, sleep sessions) against a documented threshold (default 26 hours), a stale_copy state when this machine holds an older copy than the phone last wrote, age, as_of, last data date, per-file write times.

tools.name: list_metrics
tools.description: Every available metric with unit, day count, date range.

tools.name: get_health_metrics
tools.description: Daily values for a metric over a date range, with an aggregate.

tools.name: get_trends
tools.description: Recent N-day window vs the prior N days, change, % change, direction.

tools.name: compare_periods
tools.description: A metric across two arbitrary date periods (A vs B).

tools.name: get_structured_export
tools.description: Clean JSON for chosen metrics/range for an agent's context.

tools.name: get_intraday
tools.description: The hour-by-hour window from the app's hourly automations (health-intraday.json, app 1.4+): yesterday and today, with the hour's Min and Max for discrete metrics when the app writes them. Replaced on every run: a live recent view, not history.

tools.name: query_health_data
tools.description: Natural-language convenience query routed to structured results.

tools.name: list_events
tools.description: Logged context events (medication, habit, visit, life, shift, episode, travel) from the app and from add_event, each labelled source app or agent, with type/tag/date filters.

tools.name: add_event
tools.description: Log a context event the user states (medication start, habit change, visit, trip) into health-events-agent.json; idempotent by clientEventId. The only file this server writes.

tools.name: remove_event
tools.description: Remove an event logged with add_event (id starting agent-); events logged in the iOS app are edited there.

tools.name: get_profile
tools.description: Opted-in context fields (conditions, medications, goals). Absent fields were withheld, never "none".

tools.name: get_workouts
tools.description: Query workouts by activity/date with pagination; includes heart rate, running dynamics and intervals when exported.

tools.name: get_sleep_sessions
tools.description: Clustered sleep sessions attributed to the waking day; split nights returned as separate sessions, duplicate copies of one night collapsed (collapsedDuplicates).

tools.name: get_cycle_context
tools.description: Day-in-cycle and coarse phase derived from logged period starts. Never predictive.

tools.name: correlate_metrics
tools.description: Pearson correlation between two metrics with 0..3 day lag; association, not causation.

tools.name: resolve_metric
tools.description: Canonical metric name and unit for any spelling or alias, with unit conversion; ambiguous names are never guessed.

health_data_dir.title: Apple Health export folder
health_data_dir.description: The iCloud Drive folder the MetricBridge iOS app writes to (contains .health-cache.json). On a Mac this is typically ~/Library/Mobile Documents/iCloud~ai~healthexport~app/Documents.

pairing_secret.title: Pairing code (optional)
pairing_secret.description: If you turned on Agent pairing in the iOS app (Settings → Agent pairing), paste the code here. Leave blank if pairing is off.

export_passphrase.title: Export passphrase (optional)
export_passphrase.description: Only if you turned on Export encryption in the iOS app (Settings > Export encryption): the same passphrase. It decrypts your exports on this computer and is never sent anywhere. Leave blank if encryption is off.
